findings.title: monitor-only + expired retiresAt busy-loops the daemon and swallows the config-unavailable alert
findings.detail: The monitor-only branch returns at :1727-1729 before the pass bookkeeping at :1784-1785 (`state.lastPollAt = now` and `state.nextUsageDueAt = now + pollIntervalMs(...)`). `computeNextDelay` (quota-monitor-cli.ts:98-106) is `Math.max(0, Math.min(nextUsageDueAt, nextPaneScanDueAt, confirmDueAt) - now)`, so once `nextUsageDueAt` falls into the past it stays there forever and the delay is permanently 0. Failure scenario: `~/.flywheel/quota-monitor.json` is missing or invalid (loadQuotaMonitorConfig -> `fallback()` -> `monitorOnly: true`, quota-monitor-config.ts:52-58), or the operator ran `setup-quota-monitor.sh monitor-only` (order: []), and the active account's `retiresAt` has passed. Within at most basePollMinutes the loop starts spinning with zero delay: every iteration calls `deps.reconcileActive()` and `deps.withAccountsLock(() => deps.readSnapshot())`, which takes the shared `claude-accounts.lock` and spawns `security find-generic-password` (readKeychainMonitorCredential) — pegging a core, hammering the keychain, and starving every other writer of the accounts lock (quota-guard, claude-profile, manual switches). It is also unobservable: the `deps.config.error` -> "Claude quota monitor configuration is unavailable" alert lives at :1786-1794, after this return, so it is never emitted, and this branch raises no alert about the retirement either (the 60-minute warning only fires while `activeRetirementMs > now`). Quota observation stops permanently too, so capacity/statusline silently rot.
findings.failure_scenario: quota-monitor.json missing/invalid (or installed in monitor-only mode) + active account past its retiresAt: after nextUsageDueAt elapses, pollOnce returns at :1728 every iteration with computeNextDelay()==0, so the daemon busy-loops forever, re-acquiring the accounts lock and re-spawning `security find-generic-password` each turn, while never emitting the config-unavailable alert and never recording another quota observation.

findings.title: All three retirement returns skip `state.lastPollAt = now`, so the installer boots out a healthy daemon
findings.detail: `state.lastPollAt = now` at :1784 is the only assignment to lastPollAt in the file (verified by grep). All three new retirement exits — monitor-only (:1728), the throttled retry (:1740) and the handleAccountDead call (:1748-1751) — return before it, so lastPollAt is frozen for as long as the active account is past its retiresAt. `scripts/setup-quota-monitor.sh:309-328` gates daemon health on `last_poll >= health_start_ms && now_ms - last_poll <= base_poll_ms` within HEALTH_TIMEOUT (default 90s) and on failure runs `launchctl bootout` + `die health_failed` — tearing down what the script itself calls "the only auto-switch executor ... NO Bridge fallback exists (FLY-1456)". The window is not narrow: pass 1 after bootstrap takes the retirement branch (nextUsageDueAt migrates to 0, quota-monitor-state.ts:1076, so pass 1 is usage-due) and pass 2 (paneScanSeconds default 60s later) hits the local_scan early return at :1770 because the retirement branch just pushed nextUsageDueAt 20 minutes out — neither pass refreshes lastPollAt inside the 90s gate. If the switch cannot find a target (`no_account`), lastPollAt is frozen indefinitely and the monitor can never be re-installed. This is precisely the operator flow the handoff documents (write retiresAt, restart the monitor), and the case where you most need the installer is when the monitor is already down and the active account has retired.
findings.failure_scenario: Active account is past retiresAt and the monitor is down; operator runs `scripts/setup-quota-monitor.sh enable`. The daemon boots, pass 1 switches away from the retired account (returns at :1751 without setting lastPollAt), pass 2 returns local_scan; after 90s the health loop still sees a stale lastPollAt, so the script runs `launchctl bootout` and dies with health_failed — the auto-switch daemon ends up uninstalled even though the retirement switch worked.

findings.title: Retirement reuses whatever `unavailable` mark already exists instead of the first retirement mark
findings.detail: The intent (plan R4: "retry 复用首次退休 unavailable 标记，保留原 markedAt") is to reuse the retirement mark on retries. The code instead reuses *any* pre-existing `unavailable` on the active account without checking its reason. That state is reachable: on `outcome: "no_account"` switch-executor.ts:1033-1036 writes the dead mark while the account stays active, so an account quarantined for e.g. `profile_canceled` or `usage_forbidden:...` can still be the active account when its retiresAt passes. The store then never records `reason=retirement` / the retirement evidence, and `markAccountUnavailable` (account-store.ts:287-288) no-ops on the identical mark, so no generation bump either. Diagnostics and the guard's `unavailable-clear` audit trail attribute the quarantine to the stale cause. Suggest gating the reuse on `existing?.reason === "retirement"`.
findings.failure_scenario: business is marked unavailable with reason=profile_canceled after a no_account dead-switch attempt and stays active; its retiresAt then passes. handleAccountDead reuses the profile_canceled mark, so the store/audit trail never shows that business was retired.

findings.title: Switch notification drops the 原账号/新账号 labels whenever retiresAt is set
findings.detail: When `input.from.retiresAt` / `input.to.retiresAt` is present the branch substitutes `formatAccountQuotaBlock(...)`, which renders only `**name** · email · 到期 MM-DD` plus the table — the `原账号` / `新账号` labels are gone. If both accounts carry retiresAt, neither block is labelled and the reader must map blocks to roles by name from the headline; if only one carries it, the message mixes two different layouts in the same notification. Nothing forces the label to be dropped — `formatAccountQuotaBlock` could be prefixed with the same `原账号`/`新账号` line unconditionally, which would also remove the branch. No test asserts the labels survive (switch-executor.test.ts only asserts the body contains "到期").
findings.failure_scenario: Both business and school have retiresAt configured; the account_switched notification renders two structurally identical blocks with no 原账号/新账号 marker, so the founder cannot tell which account was left and which was entered except by re-reading the headline.

findings.title: panoramaBody grew ~7x per account with no truncation on the 2000-char Discord path
findings.detail: `panoramaBody` went from one ~30-char line per account to a ~220-char block (heading + fenced 6-line table + 状态 line). Nothing on the delivery path truncates: `scripts/lead-alert.sh:612-621` builds CONTENT from BODY verbatim and posts it (no length guard anywhere in lead-alert.sh or LeadAlertNotifier), and `setNoTargetContext` (quota-monitor.ts:828) caps `episode.detail` at 4000 bytes — double Discord's 2000-char content limit — before `buildNoTargetBody` appends more. With today's 5-account pool a quota_no_target body lands around 1.2-1.4k, i.e. ~30% headroom; adding pool members or longer status strings pushes it past 2000 and Discord answers 400, losing the founder's only "no verified Claude account has quota" alert. Suggest capping the rendered panorama (e.g. cap blocks and fall back to the one-line form beyond N accounts) rather than relying on pool size staying at 5.
findings.failure_scenario: The account pool grows to ~9 entries and all keys are exhausted: the quota_no_target body exceeds Discord's 2000-char content limit, the POST returns HTTP 400, and the severe "no verified account has quota" alert is never delivered.

findings.title: Retirement check reads the full snapshot (keychain subprocess + pool listing) on every 60s pass
findings.detail: The snapshot read was moved ahead of the local_scan early return, so `deps.withAccountsLock(() => deps.readSnapshot())` now runs on every pane pass (paneScanSeconds default 60) instead of only on usage-due passes (basePollMinutes default 20). `readSnapshot` (quota-monitor-runtime.ts:539-553) does `readStore` + `resolveMachineAccount` + `await readKeychain()` (spawning `security find-generic-password`, quota-monitor-credentials.ts:51-76) + `listPoolAccounts`, all while the shared `claude-accounts.lock` is held — a 20x increase in subprocess spawns and in lock-hold time that every other account-store writer contends with. The retirement check only needs `accounts[].retiresAt` and the machine authority, both of which a plain store/identity read provides; consider a cheap read for the early check and keeping the full snapshot where it was.
findings.failure_scenario: On a busy host the monitor now holds the accounts lock across a `security` subprocess once per minute rather than once per 20 minutes, so concurrent flywheel-quota-guard / claude-profile / manual-switch writers block on the lock ~20x more often for no functional gain.

findings.title: --plain-message opened to every quota_monitor_down producer, not just retirement warnings
findings.detail: The guard right below the FLY-2051 comment ("ordinary-message rendering is a narrow capability, not a generic way for alert producers to bypass ticket/alert framing") now allows `--plain-message` for the whole `quota_monitor_down` kind, and `PLAIN_DELIVERY_KINDS` in LeadAlertNotifier.ts:391-396 does the same for queued delivery. The only narrowing to retirement lives in a single caller (quota-monitor-alert.ts:218-220, `signature.startsWith("account-retirement-")`), i.e. the boundary check is coarser than the policy it is supposed to enforce. Since plain delivery also skips the ticket/thread lifecycle (LeadAlertNotifier.ts:1411), any future quota_monitor_down producer that passes --plain-message silently loses its ticket. Suggest keying the allowlist on the signature prefix (or a dedicated alert kind) in both the shell guard and PLAIN_DELIVERY_KINDS so it matches the documented intent.
findings.failure_scenario: A later quota_monitor_down producer (e.g. the config-unavailable alert) is given --plain-message; both guards accept it, the message renders with no title/severity header and never opens a ticket or thread, so the monitor-down condition is never tracked to closure.

findings.title: A typo in the hand-edited retiresAt silently removes an account from the switch pool with no alert
findings.detail: `retiresAt` is written by hand into `~/.flywheel/claude-accounts.json` (the handoff explicitly leaves this to Lead/QA and the setter CLI is a deferred follow-up), and `readStoreStrict` (account-store.ts:698-731) does not validate it at all — unlike quotaExhaustedUntil/weeklyResetAt/switchCooldownUntil/unavailable. Any malformed value (`"2026-09-14"`, `"...-0700"`, or JSON `null`, which is `typeof "object"` and returns NaN) makes `retirementMs` NaN, and both selector paths (account-candidate-selector.ts:193-201, account-store.ts:506/541) then exclude the account permanently. Nothing alerts on it: the `retirement_malformed` status only surfaces inside a panorama during an actual switch attempt, and the account keeps rendering in the patrol capacity line as if it had no retirement (hook-payload passes retiresAt straight to formatAccountQuotaBlock, which silently omits the 到期 suffix on a NaN). A five-account pool can silently shrink to one with the founder seeing nothing until the next switch fails. Suggest validating retiresAt in readStoreStrict (or emitting a dedicated alert when a pool entry has a malformed retiresAt).
findings.failure_scenario: An operator writes "retiresAt": "2026-09-14" (date-only) on school and shopping. Both are permanently excluded from candidate selection and no alert is raised; the patrol capacity line still shows them as healthy, and the first quota switch after that reports "No verified Claude account has quota".

findings.title: `retirementLabel` is exported dead code
findings.detail: `retirementLabel` has no callers anywhere in `packages/` or `scripts/` (only its own definition and the compiled `dist/` copy). The 到期 suffix is produced instead by `formatAccountQuotaBlock` via `resetTimestamp(...).slice(0, 5)`. Per the repo's dead-code-hygiene rule it should be removed or wired up; leaving two competing retirement-date formatters invites divergence (the unused one renders `(9-14 到期)`, the live one renders `到期 09-14`).
findings.failure_scenario: A later change updates only one of the two retirement-date formatters, so the patrol line and whatever adopts retirementLabel disagree on the displayed expiry format.

findings.title: Patrol tick capacity section grows from one line to ~8 lines per account
findings.detail: `renderValidCapacityLines` now emits a heading + fenced 6-line table + 观测 line per Claude account (plus a blank separator) instead of one `name 5h x%/7d y%(age)` token per account joined by ` · `. For the 5-account production pool that turns a single ~60-char line into roughly 40 lines / ~1.1k chars, injected into every Lead context on every patrol tick (mailbox-lead-runtime.ts:225, commdb-lead-runtime.ts:100) with no size cap in hook-payload. The `Fable` row is additionally always `n/a n/a n/a` here because the capacity snapshot carries no `raw` quota (quotaTable falls back to null when `usage.raw` is absent), so a third of each table is pure noise. Worth confirming with the founder that the per-tick token cost is intended, and consider dropping the Fable row when `raw` is unavailable.
findings.failure_scenario: Every patrol tick for every Lead carries ~1.1k extra characters of capacity tables, a third of it constant `Fable n/a n/a n/a` rows, increasing per-tick context cost with no added signal.
